issues.title: Cycle 1 retro's '14 dormant renderers / 14 missing event-type branches' framing overcounts the work by ~3x
issues.description: The cycle 1 retro (plan_vs_outcome + protocol_blocked_summary) and the cycle 2 test plan state that extending codexAppServerClient.ts to emit 14 new event types will activate 14 dormant renderers. Ground truth from `codex app-server generate-ts`: the 14 tool types collapse onto ~5 `ThreadItem` variants (plan, mcpToolCall, dynamicToolCall, collabAgentToolCall, optional imageView). One item-type branch (collabAgentToolCall) covers all 5 subagent verbs via the CollabAgentTool enum. One item-type branch (dynamicToolCall) covers tool_suggest + multi_tool_use.parallel + write_stdin + request_user_input + view_image. So the real codexAppServerClient.ts delta is ~5 branches, not 14. The real sessionProtocolMapper.ts delta is ~5-6 paired begin/end branches, not 14 pairs. This is SMALLER and CLEANER than the test plan assumes — but requires correcting the framing for BA and Dev.

issues.title: Path B (mapper-only synthesis from agentMessage) is factually not viable — line 364 silent-consume blocks it
issues.description: The orchestrator's question D asks whether sessionProtocolMapper.ts can synthesize the missing tool-call envelopes from existing `agentMessage` payloads (e.g., if the Codex agentMessage carries `input.tool_uses[]`). Examining ThreadItem.agentMessage schema: {type:'agentMessage', id:string, text:string, phase:MessagePhase|null, memoryCitation:MemoryCitation|null}. agentMessage is plain text only — no nested tool_uses, no input blob. Furthermore, codexAppServerClient.ts:364 `return method.startsWith('item/')` silently returns true for ALL unhandled item/* methods BEFORE the event handler fires. So the 5 subagent verbs (collabAgentToolCall), 4 Phase B verbs (dynamicToolCall), 3 MCP verbs (mcpToolCall) never reach the mapper today regardless of what logic the mapper contains. Path B is structurally unreachable — Dev must NOT pursue it. The test plan's architectural question D should be retracted.

issues.title: EventMsg discriminator naming contract must be decided BEFORE Dev starts — rework cost is high
issues.description: The current 3 branches use per-verb discriminator names (exec_command_begin, exec_command_end, patch_apply_begin, patch_apply_end, agent_message). Two options for the 5 new item.type branches: (Option 1) One EventMsg discriminator per verb — e.g. spawn_agent_begin/end, send_input_begin/end, wait_agent_begin/end × 5 + dynamic tools × 5 + MCP verbs × 3 — bloats to ~26 event-type strings. (Option 2) One EventMsg discriminator per item.type family — collab_agent_call_begin/end carries item.tool CollabAgentTool enum; dynamic_tool_call_begin/end carries item.namespace+item.tool; mcp_tool_call_begin/end carries item.server+item.tool — total ~8-10 new event types. Mapper must decode the tool name accordingly. If codexAppServerClient and sessionProtocolMapper disagree on this contract, Dev will rewrite twice. Architect RECOMMENDS Option 2 — the mapper already does this kind of string synthesis (see commandToTitle at line 132 of sessionProtocolMapper.ts).
issues.observation_notes: Read both files fully. exec_command_begin/end pattern is the existing template — mapper's pickCallId() + commandToTitle() + args-splatting at lines 295-314 shows the shape. issues.title: Daemon restart cgroup-kill risk — explicit procedure MUST be in pipeline spec
issues.description: CLAUDE.md rule 5: 'NEVER restart daemon from within a daemon-managed Claude session (cgroup kill)'. Cycle 2 primary task requires daemon rebuild + restart after source change. If Dev (running inside the orchestrator's daemon-managed session) runs `systemctl restart happy-daemon-dev` directly, the cgroup kill terminates the orchestrator session. Must use: `systemd-run --scope -- systemctl restart happy-daemon-dev.service` OR `nohup bash -c 'sleep 2 && systemctl restart happy-daemon-dev.service' < /dev/null > /dev/null 2>&1 &` to detach. BA must write this into the pipeline spec step explicitly — cycle 1's §5.9 hit this trap in close-remediation.

architecture_proposals.title: Introduce a single `emitToolCallItem()` helper in codexAppServerClient to dispatch item.type branches
architecture_proposals.current_state: codexAppServerClient.ts:280-362 has 3 parallel if-blocks (commandExecution, fileChange, agentMessage), each hand-rolling the `item.id → callId` extraction and EventMsg construction. Each new item.type branch would duplicate this pattern. With 5+ new branches, duplication grows linearly.
architecture_proposals.proposed_state: Extract a private `emitItemEvent(method: string, item: ThreadItem, beginType: string, endType: string, extraFields: (item) => Record<string, unknown>)` helper. Each existing and new branch becomes a one-liner dispatch. This is a REFACTOR of lines 280-362 done in the SAME pipeline as the extension — keeps the file consistent and cuts the ~120 new LOC roughly in half.
architecture_proposals.measurable_benefit: Reduces codexAppServerClient.ts added LOC from ~120 to ~60 (50% reduction); eliminates 3 instances of duplicated 'const callId = typeof item.id === string ? item.id : ...' boilerplate; makes adding future item.type branches (e.g. webSearch, imageGeneration when §5.15 Phase A expands) trivial.
architecture_proposals.risk_if_ignored: Each future Codex tool family extension adds 20-30 LOC of duplicated dispatch plumbing. Over 5+ cycles this compounds into hundreds of duplicated lines, each a potential refactor-drift bug.
architecture_proposals.migration_strategy: Internal refactor — no external API change. Dev can write the helper, then rewrite the 3 existing branches to use it + the 5 new branches. Tests in codexAppServerClient.test.ts verify behavior unchanged.

architecture_proposals.title: Tighten the EventMsg type to a discriminated union instead of `{type: string} & Record<string, unknown>`
architecture_proposals.current_state: codexAppServerTypes.ts:152 defines EventMsg as `{ type: string } & Record<string, unknown>` — a loose Record that accepts any string as type discriminator and any extra fields. Consumers (runCodex.ts:434-527, sessionProtocolMapper.ts:179-388) must cast `msg as any` to read fields, losing type safety.
architecture_proposals.proposed_state: Replace with a discriminated union enumerating the known event types: `type EventMsg = {type:'task_started', turn_id?:string} | {type:'task_complete', ...} | {type:'agent_message', message:string, item_id?, phase?} | {type:'exec_command_begin', call_id, callId, command, cwd, description} | ... | {type:'collab_agent_call_begin', ...} | ...`. Add an `unknown` fallback variant for future extensibility: `| {type:string, [key:string]:unknown}` as last element of the union.
architecture_proposals.measurable_benefit: Enables TypeScript exhaustiveness checks in sessionProtocolMapper.ts. Eliminates ~10 `as any` casts in runCodex.ts:438-508. Catches field-name typos at compile time — currently `msg.turn_id` vs `msg.turnId` mismatches pass typecheck silently.
architecture_proposals.risk_if_ignored: Each new event type added to codexAppServerClient must be manually reflected in every consumer; drift accumulates. Cycle 2 adds 5+ event types; cycle 3's §5.10 and future Codex phases add more.
architecture_proposals.migration_strategy: Additive — the new union is compatible with existing `{type:string} & Record<string,unknown>` usage because the fallback variant preserves the loose shape. Dev can land this in a separate follow-up pipeline after cycle 2's primary fix.
